## Create SpatialData objects

This code is inspired by [this tutorial](https://spatialdata.scverse.org/en/latest/tutorials/notebooks/notebooks/examples/alignment_using_landmarks.html).

```{python}
import numpy as np
import spatialdata as sd

from napari_spatialdata import Interactive
import spatialdata_io as sio
import spatialdata_plot

c26t16 = sio.visium(path="data/Sample_S54409_C26Sh_16_18_20/outs/", dataset_id="C26T16", fullres_image_file = "../../Spatial_Omics_IHC_161820_Merged_ch00.tif")
c26t16

c26t16.pl.render_images().pl.render_shapes().pl.show("downscaled_lowres")
```

Let's add the images.

```{python}
from dask_image.imread import imread
from xarray import DataArray
from spatialdata.models import Image2DModel
from spatialdata.models import PointsModel
from spatialdata.transformations.transformations import Identity

image = imread("data/IF_WGA_dapi_GFP/Slide161820_GFP.ome.tif").squeeze().transpose(2, 0, 1)
image = DataArray(image, dims=("c", "y", "x"))

im_mod = Image2DModel.parse(
    image,
    scale_factors=[2, 2, 2, 2],
    transformations={"global": Identity()}
    )

c26t16.add_image(name="C26T16_GFP", image=im_mod)

image = imread("data/IF_WGA_dapi_GFP/Project_C26 sh 16_18_20_merge.tif").squeeze().transpose(2, 0, 1)
image = DataArray(image, dims=("c", "y", "x"))

im_mod = Image2DModel.parse(
    image,
    scale_factors=[2, 2, 2, 2],
    transformations={"global": Identity()}
    )

c26t16.add_image(name="C26T16_merge", image=im_mod)
```

## Visualize with Napari

In this interactive chunk, I add the landmarks.

```{python}
#| eval: false
Interactive(c26t16)
```

```{python}
sdata = sd.read_zarr("c26t16.zarr/")
sdata.points
c26t16.add_points("IF landmarks", PointsModel.parse(sdata.points["IF landmarks"]))
c26t16.add_points("Visium landmarks", PointsModel.parse(sdata.points["Visium landmarks"]))
```

Now we can transform the images.

```{python}
from spatialdata.transformations import (
    align_elements_using_landmarks,
    set_transformation,
)
from spatialdata import save_transformations

affine = align_elements_using_landmarks(
    references_coords=c26t16["IF landmarks"],
    moving_coords=c26t16["Visium landmarks"],
    reference_element=c26t16["C26T16_GFP"],
    moving_element=c26t16["C26T16_full_image"],
    reference_coordinate_system="global",
    moving_coordinate_system="global",
    new_coordinate_system="aligned",
)
affine

set_transformation(c26t16["C26T16"], affine, "aligned")
# save_transformations(c26t16)
```

```{python}
c26t16 = c26t16.transform_to_coordinate_system("aligned")
```

Let's save the object in .zarr file.

```{python}
c26t16.write("c26t16_align.zarr")
```
